title: Grateful Dead Live at Compton Terrace Amphitheatre on 1982-07-25
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell UDXLII-C90/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: Solid setlist with emotional Lost Sailor and groovy Samson, captured on a decent audience recording using Sennheiser 421s
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its strong set list – highlights include the Half‑Step opener, the seamless Black Peter → Good Lovin' transition, an tear‑jerking Lost Sailor, and a funky Samson. Recording-wise it’s an audience tape recorded with Sennheiser 421 microphones; listeners note good overall balance but a slight lack of cymbal detail.

ai_rating.rationale: Three reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise the performance, while one low rating focuses on mic characteristics; overall the musical show is strong and the audience recording is acceptable.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear enough for a full‑band mix, but Sennheiser 421 mics capture less cymbal detail; overall considered spot‑on by most listeners.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Solid pacing with a strong second half; smooth transitions keep the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s spontaneous line about "freedom not comin' easy" and coffee during Lost Sailor was a fan‑favorite moment.
